new_candidates.body:
## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (Noble), amd64 and arm64.
- Binary install: ROS 2 Jazzy's `ros-jazzy-simulation`, i.e. Gazebo Harmonic. In today's packages.ros.org Noble index that resolves to:
  - `ros-jazzy-gz-sim-vendor` 0.0.13, which is gz-sim 8.15.0;
  - `ros-jazzy-gz-common-vendor` 0.0.10, which is gz-common 5.9.0;
  - `ros-jazzy-gz-transport-vendor` 0.0.9, which is gz-transport 13.6.0.
- Runs headless (`gz sim -s`), several servers at once, each in its own `GZ_PARTITION`, all sharing one `$HOME`.
- The image is `ghcr.io/partcad/partcad-sim-gazebo`: `ros:jazzy-ros-base` plus `ros-jazzy-simulation`.

## Description

If a world has no `<plugin>` elements, the server loads its default systems through `gz::sim::loadPluginInfo()`.

`loadPluginInfo()` reads `~/.gz/sim/8/server.config`:
- If that file doesn't exist, it first copies the installed `server.config` there.
- The check and the copy are not atomic.
- `common::copyFile()` is `std::filesystem::copy_file(..., overwrite_existing)`. That creates (or truncates) the destination and then writes into it.

So when several servers start at once with a fresh `$HOME`:

1. Server A sees no `~/.gz/sim/8/server.config` and starts copying the installed file there.
2. Server B checks a moment later. The file exists, but it's still empty or partly written. Server B parses it straight away.
3. tinyxml2 finds no root element, so server B logs:
   ```
   [Err] [ServerConfig.cc:824] No <server_config> element found when parsing plugins
   ```
4. `loadPluginInfo()` returns an empty list.
5. Server B carries on with **no systems at all**:
   - no Physics;
   - no SceneBroadcaster, so nothing is published on `/world/<name>/pose/info` and nothing is ever going to be;
   - no UserCommands.

   The process stays alive and keeps answering on `/world/<name>/control`, so a client sees a server that is up and simply never publishes.

There is a second interleaving of the same race. Two servers both see the file missing and both copy. The second one's `O_TRUNC` empties the file while the first one is parsing it.

The same check makes a half-written file permanent:
- Suppose the server doing the copy is killed partway through, for example by a test timeout.
- The empty or truncated file stays in place.
- Every later server in that home sees that it exists, parses it, and runs with no systems.
- This goes on until somebody deletes it.

The server never reports either case as an error. All it emits is the `[Err]` line above and the warning "Loaded config: [...], but no plugins found". In a batch of runs that start together, the result is one server in a handful that hangs, and which one varies from run to run.

### Where in the code

All references are at gz-sim `gz-sim8` b791db8dd6fecf85f191a8796ff2dd817f951c07. Tag `gz-sim8_8.15.0` (446a44335a45b704b4d36dabcc5508ee34eeb3d8) has the same line numbers.

- `src/ServerConfig.cc`, `sim::loadPluginInfo()` ([L917](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/b791db8dd6fecf85f191a8796ff2dd817f951c07/src/ServerConfig.cc#L917)):
  - the existence check is at [L989](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/b791db8dd6fecf85f191a8796ff2dd817f951c07/src/ServerConfig.cc#L989);
  - the copy is at [L1010](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/b791db8dd6fecf85f191a8796ff2dd817f951c07/src/ServerConfig.cc#L1010);
  - the parse of the copied file is at [L1025](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/b791db8dd6fecf85f191a8796ff2dd817f951c07/src/ServerConfig.cc#L1025).
- `src/ServerConfig.cc`, `parsePluginsFromDoc()`: [L818-L826](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/b791db8dd6fecf85f191a8796ff2dd817f951c07/src/ServerConfig.cc#L818-L826). This is where a null root produces the error and an empty list.
- `src/SimulationRunner.cc`: [L1769-L1777](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/b791db8dd6fecf85f191a8796ff2dd817f951c07/src/SimulationRunner.cc#L1769-L1777). With no world systems loaded it loads the defaults, which here is an empty list, and nothing checks for that.
- gz-common `gz-common5` 106b2b0bc16c581433f0d0992144363e3a3c55fd, `src/Filesystem.cc`, `common::copyFile()`: [L238-L247](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-common/blob/106b2b0bc16c581433f0d0992144363e3a3c55fd/src/Filesystem.cc#L238-L247). It is `fs::copy_file(..., fs::copy_options::overwrite_existing)`, with no temporary file and no rename.

The same code is still on the newer branches:
- `gz-sim10` 8f34c8b04a1780de36c6d4d559797bafe710d57d: [ServerConfig.cc L997/L1018/L1033](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/8f34c8b04a1780de36c6d4d559797bafe710d57d/src/ServerConfig.cc#L997-L1033).
- `main` dad15e230aecc0c685b8a56db8a593f65e213c7c: [ServerConfig.cc L997/L1018/L1033](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/dad15e230aecc0c685b8a56db8a593f65e213c7c/src/ServerConfig.cc#L997-L1033).

On `main` the defaults are also loaded when the `include_server_config_plugins` policy is set ([SimulationRunner.cc L1919-L1925](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/dad15e230aecc0c685b8a56db8a593f65e213c7c/src/SimulationRunner.cc#L1919-L1925)), so the race reaches that case as well.

The GUI does the same copy of `gui.config`, unguarded in the same way: `src/gui/Gui.cc` [L83-L98 on gz-sim8](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/b791db8dd6fecf85f191a8796ff2dd817f951c07/src/gui/Gui.cc#L83-L98) and [L200-L215 on main](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/dad15e230aecc0c685b8a56db8a593f65e213c7c/src/gui/Gui.cc#L200-L215). We haven't hit it there, since we run headless.

## Steps to reproduce

This is what our CI does: several servers within the same second, each with its own partition, sharing a `$HOME` that has no `.gz` directory yet.

```bash
export HOME=$(mktemp -d)          # GZ_HOMEDIR is HOME on Linux; no ~/.gz yet
cat > nosystems.sdf <<'EOF'
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<sdf version="1.9"><world name="w"></world></sdf>
EOF
# A world with no <plugin> elements, so the server falls back to server.config.
# (worlds/empty.sdf lists its own plugins and does not exercise this path.)
for i in $(seq 1 8); do
  GZ_PARTITION=p$i timeout 20 gz sim -s -v 4 nosystems.sdf > server$i.log 2>&1 &
done
wait
grep -l "Copied installed config" server*.log        # the ones that copied
grep -l "No <server_config> element found" server*.log   # the ones that read it half-written
```

Then repeat with a fresh `HOME`.

We ran this script in the image above (gz-sim 8.15.0) on a 32-core amd64 host: 10 trials, 5 with 8 servers and 5 with 16, each trial with a fresh `HOME`.

- In 5 of the 10 trials, more than one server logged `Copied installed config` (up to 6 servers in one trial). That is the check-then-copy race itself, even when nobody happens to read the file mid-copy.
- In 1 of the 10 trials, a server logged `No <server_config> element found when parsing plugins` and then `Loaded config: [...], but no plugins found`. In that trial 4 servers had copied the file.

So the window is short, and whether a run hits it depends on how many servers start at once and how loaded the machine is. A busy CI runner makes it more likely.

## Expected behavior

Every server loads the default systems in `server.config`, however many of them start at once.

## Actual behavior

Some of the servers log `No <server_config> element found when parsing plugins` and run with no systems. They stay alive, answer the control service, and never publish poses or anything else a system would.

The same thing happened to us in CI, on an `ubuntu-latest` runner:
- [partcad/partcad run 40120022592, job 120956979240](https://github.com/partcad/partcad/actions/runs/40120022592/job/120956979240)
- The server's stderr contains `[Err] [ServerConfig.cc:824] No <server_config> element found when parsing plugins`.
- No pose ever arrived on `/world/<name>/pose/info` for that run.

## Suggested fix

Make creating `~/.gz/sim/<N>/server.config` (and `gui.config`) atomic, so that a reader sees either no file or the whole file:

- Copy to a temporary file in the same directory, e.g. `server.config.<pid>.tmp`, and then `rename()` it over `server.config`.
  - On POSIX that rename is atomic.
  - On Windows, `MoveFileEx(..., MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)` or `std::filesystem::rename`.
  - A server that loses the race just finds the complete file. If the rename fails because the file is already there, that isn't an error either.
- Alternatively, parse the **installed** file when the user's copy doesn't exist yet. Make the copy into `~/.gz` a best-effort side effect that never affects what this server loads.

A `copyFileAtomic()` in gz-common, or an option on `copyFile()`, would serve both call sites. It would also serve anything else that seeds a user config from an installed one.

Separately, it would help to make "the server config could not be parsed, so this server has no systems" loud. That covers an empty list from a file that exists but has no root element. Today it's indistinguishable from a deliberate empty config, apart from one `[Err]` line.

## Workaround

When `~/.gz/sim/8/server.config` doesn't exist yet, or exists but is empty or unreadable, we start the server with `GZ_SIM_SERVER_CONFIG_PATH` pointing at the installed `server.config`. The server then reads that file where it is, with no copy into `~`. We find it through `GZ_CONFIG_PATH` and the `share/gz` next to the `gz` binary (`gz-sim*/server.config`). A user's existing, valid copy is left alone. We also fail a run fast when the `[Err]` line above appears, rather than waiting for poses that will never come. See [partcad/partcad-sim-gazebo#19](https://github.com/partcad/partcad-sim-gazebo/pull/19) (e16f908).

Creating `~/.gz/sim/8/server.config` once before starting any servers in parallel also works.
new_candidates.title: Servers started at the same time with a fresh `$HOME` can read a half-copied `server.config` and run with no systems
